h1:
Aiyerweng Skywalk Review
A glass floor over the southernmost sea of mist in Betong
intro: Aiyerweng Skywalk is the landmark that put Thailand's deep south back on the map for travelers nationwide. This viewpoint sits on Microwave Mountain, in Ai Yer Weng subdistrict, Betong district, Yala province, at an elevation of roughly 2,038 feet above sea level. The highlight is a walkway that juts out from the cliffside, ending in a clear glass floor you can look straight down through to see the sea of mist floating below. It's known as one of the few viewpoints in Thailand where you can catch a sea of mist almost year-round, at its most beautiful from March to April. In this review we go in-depth on the glass-floor skywalk itself, the early-morning routine of waking up to catch the sunrise, the ticket price and hilltop shuttle, all the way through to pairing it with the Piyamit Tunnel, hot springs, and the cool-climate flower garden for a full one-day Betong trip.

blocks.html:
If you ask what image comes to mind first when people talk about visiting Betong these days, the answer is almost always the Aiyerweng Skywalk — a glass-floor walkway jutting out from the ridge of Microwave Mountain, its far end suspended above the valley, where on a good morning a white sea of mist fills the space below until you feel like you're standing on a cloud. The spot sits in Ai Yer Weng subdistrict, about 30 kilometers north of Betong town along a winding mountain road, and it's become the main reason people are willing to travel all the way to Thailand's southernmost district.

What sets Aiyerweng apart from other sea-of-mist viewpoints is how consistent it is. Thanks to the humid valley terrain and its proximity to the Bang Lang Dam reservoir, the sea of mist appears here almost year-round — you don't have to wait specifically for the cool season like at other spots. In this review, we'll go in-depth on the experience of climbing up to the Aiyerweng Skywalk, covering both what makes people fall in love with it and what to brace yourself for before you actually go, along with how to plan a Betong itinerary that makes the trip worthwhile.

blocks.descHtml:
Aiyerweng Skywalk is a viewing walkway built to jut out from the ridge of Microwave Mountain, in Ai Yer Weng subdistrict, Betong district, at its highest point roughly 2,038 feet above sea level. The structure is a long walkway whose far end forms a clear glass-floor platform — standing on the glass, you can look straight down and see the valley and the sea of mist below, giving the sensation of floating in midair. All around are the mountain ranges of the Hala-Bala forest and the area surrounding the Bang Lang Dam reservoir, opening up sweeping views in nearly every direction.

The real draw here is the sea of mist. Thanks to the high humidity from the surrounding forest and nearby reservoir, Aiyerweng sees a sea of mist almost year-round, unlike mountains in the north where mist tends to appear only in the cool season. The mist is thickest and most beautiful roughly from March to April. The highlight of a visit here is waking up well before dawn, driving up or taking the shuttle to arrive before first light, then standing and watching the sun slowly rise above a sea of mist that shifts color as the light changes. Many say it's a sight well worth getting up at four or five in the morning for.

Based on real reviews from people who've been, the Aiyerweng Sea of Mist viewpoint gets fairly high praise on Tripadvisor, averaging around 4.5 out of 5. The recurring theme is that the sea of mist is more beautiful than expected, and the glass-floor skywalk offers an experience that's hard to find elsewhere in Thailand. On the downside, you do have to wake up before dawn, and the mountain air is cold and windy, so a warm jacket is a must. The viewpoint itself has parking down below, and you then have to transfer to a shuttle for the rest of the way up. On long holiday weekends it gets crowded and you may have to queue for the shuttle. On days with low humidity or rain, you might not see the mist as hoped for — a matter of nature that's simply beyond anyone's control. Importantly, Betong is a remote district reached by winding mountain roads, so plan your route in advance and check the latest travel advisories for the area before setting out.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: The viewpoint opens very early, generally around 5:30am. Try to arrive before sunrise to catch the sea of mist and the morning light at their best. Bring a warm jacket and a flashlight or phone light, since it's still dark and cold before dawn. Park in the lower lot, then take the viewpoint's shuttle up to the skywalk — allow extra time for the shuttle queue on holidays. If you don't have your own vehicle or don't want to drive up the mountain yourself, booking a Betong tour that includes shuttle transport lets you fit Aiyerweng and other sights into a single trip.

blocks.title: What to know before visiting Aiyerweng Skywalk

items.title: Go before dawn for sunrise
items.text: The viewpoint opens very early, generally around 5:30am. The heart of the experience is the sea of mist and morning light, so arrive before first light to catch the sunrise over the mist. Bring a flashlight or phone light, since it's still dark beforehand and the path may be slippery with dew.

items.title: Dress warm
items.text: Even though this is southern Thailand, the viewpoint sits at roughly 2,038 feet elevation, and the pre-dawn air is cold and windy, especially if you're standing around waiting for the mist. Bring a warm jacket or windbreaker, and wear shoes that grip well on damp ground.

items.title: Entry fee and shuttle
items.text: Entry is generally around ฿40 for Thai nationals and around ฿200 for foreign visitors. You'll need to park your own vehicle in the lower lot and then transfer to the viewpoint's shuttle for the rest of the way up to the skywalk, which has a separate fare. Bring cash and allow extra time for the shuttle queue on holidays.

items.title: Pair it with other Betong sights
items.text: Aiyerweng is about 30 km from Betong town. After coming down from the skywalk in the late morning, many visitors continue on to the Piyamit Tunnel, Betong hot springs, the cool-climate flower garden, and the postbox/landmarks in central Betong. It's easy to plan as a one- or two-day trip. Betong is a popular domestic destination that people tend to explore over several days, but plan your mountain driving route and check the latest travel advisories before you go.

faq.q: What time does the Aiyerweng Skywalk open?
faq.a: The viewpoint opens very early, generally around 5:30am, since the highlight is the sea of mist and sunrise. Try to arrive before first light to catch the best of the morning light and the thickest mist. Check the latest opening hours and travel advisories for the area before you go, as they may be adjusted depending on weather conditions.

faq.q: How much is the entry fee for Aiyerweng Skywalk?
faq.a: Entry to the viewpoint is generally around ฿40 for Thai nationals and around ฿200 for foreign visitors. On top of that, you'll need to take the viewpoint's shuttle up to the skywalk, which has a separate fee. Bring cash and allow extra time for the shuttle queue on holidays.

faq.q: What time of year has the most beautiful sea of mist at Aiyerweng?
faq.a: Aiyerweng sees a sea of mist almost year-round thanks to humidity from the surrounding forest and nearby reservoir, but the mist is thickest and most beautiful roughly from March to April. That said, on some days with low humidity or rain, the mist may not appear as hoped — a matter of nature that's simply beyond anyone's control.

faq.q: Do I have to drive up myself, or is there a shuttle?
faq.a: Private vehicles park in the lower lot of the viewpoint, and you then need to transfer to the viewpoint's shuttle for the rest of the way up to the skywalk, which has a separate fare. If you'd rather not drive the winding mountain road yourself before dawn, booking a Betong tour with shuttle transport is a convenient alternative.

faq.q: What other Betong sights pair well with a visit to Aiyerweng?
faq.a: Aiyerweng is about 30 km from Betong town. After coming down from the skywalk in the late morning, many visitors continue on to the Piyamit Tunnel, Betong hot springs, the cool-climate flower garden, and photo spots in central Betong. It's easy to plan as a one- or two-day trip. Betong is a popular domestic destination that people tend to explore over several days — plan your mountain driving route and check the latest travel advisories before you go.
